documents.title: About The Islamia University of Bahawalpur
documents.source: iub.edu.pk — About University, Vision & Mission, Vice Chancellor's Message
documents.text: The Islamia University of Bahawalpur (IUB) is a public sector university in Bahawalpur, Pakistan, with a history going back to 1925. It was originally established by His Highness Nawab Sir Sadiq Muhammad Khan Abbasi-V as Jamia Abbasia in 1925, upgraded as Jamia Islamia in 1963, and converted into a chartered university — The Islamia University of Bahawalpur — in 1975 under The Islamia University of Bahawalpur Act 1975. The university has seven campuses: Abbasia Campus, Baghdad-ul-Jadeed Campus and Khwaja Fareed Campus in Bahawalpur, and sub-campuses in Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Liaquatpur and Ahmedpur East. It has 135 teaching departments offering more than 300 disciplines to around 58,000 students, with more than 2,000 faculty members including 600+ PhDs. In the Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025, IUB was placed in the 800+ band worldwide; in the UI GreenMetric World University Ranking 2024 it ranked 10th among Pakistani universities and 331st worldwide. Vision: to be a world-class university with a global outlook and be a catalyst for socioeconomic transformation of the region. Mission: to produce human and intellectual capital of high socioeconomic value through top quality academic and research programs. The Vice Chancellor of the university is Prof. Dr. Muhammad Kamran. University contact: +92-62-9250235, info@iub.edu.pk.

documents.title: Scholarships & Financial Assistance at IUB
documents.source: iub.edu.pk — Scholarships, Student Support (Directorate of Financial Assistance)
documents.text: Scholarships and financial assistance at IUB are managed by the Directorate of Financial Assistance, which has financed more than 20% of the university's students through need-based scholarships and awards for high achievers. Scholarship programs listed by the university include: Ehsaas Scholarship (Benazir Undergraduate Scholarship Project), HEC Need Based Scholarship, PAK-USAID Merit and Need Based Scholarship, Pakistan Scottish Scholarship, Karwan-e-Ilm, Diya Scholarship, PEEF (Rahmatul-lil-Alameen), PEEF Master Level Scholarship, PEEF Bachelor Level Scholarship, NEST Scholarship Program, BEEF Scholarship Program, Ehsan Trust, Gilgit Baltistan Scholarship, Gwadar Scholarship, Prime Minister's Fee Reimbursement Scheme, Bait-ul-Mal Scholarships and Mora Scholarship. The university also offers fee remissions from its own resources: Needy Fee Remission, Position Holder Fee Remission, Orphan Fee Remission, Hafiz-e-Quran Fee Remission, Kinship Fee Remission, Fee Waiver Scholarship, and special scholarships for employees and their families. The Ehsaas Scholarship covers the university tuition fee and a stipend for the full 4-5 year undergraduate degree; 50% of its scholarships are reserved for female students and 2% for physically challenged students; it is for newly admitted undergraduate students admitted on merit who are not availing any other scholarship and are not enrolled on a self-finance basis. Application openings and dates are announced separately for each program — students should contact the Directorate of Financial Assistance for current announcements. Students often ask about wazifa (scholarship) at IUB — the Directorate of Financial Assistance is the office for all wazifa and scholarship matters.

documents.title: Hostel Facilities at IUB
documents.text: Hostel facility is available at IUB for boys and girls. IUB provides hostel accommodation through sixteen hostels across five campuses, with a capacity of about 10,000 students. At Abbasia Campus: Rabia Hall for girls and Abu Bakar Hall for boys. Girls hostels include Fatima-tuz-Zahra Hall, Ayesha Siddiqa Hall, Zainab Hall and Halima Hall. Boys hostels at Baghdad-ul-Jadeed Campus include Umar Hall, Ali Hall, Ahmad Hall and Usman Hall. Bahawalnagar Campus has Ayesha Hall (girls) and Abu Bakar Hall (boys); Rahim Yar Khan Campus has Ayesha Hall (girls) and Iqbal Hall (boys). Every hostel has a cafeteria, dining hall and common rooms; hostels also have computer labs, reading rooms and library facilities, indoor games, sports and gym facilities, and study parks. Hostel charges and the allotment process are not published on the university's hostel page — students should contact the hostel administration or the Directorate of Students Affairs for current hostel fees and allotment.

documents.title: Sir Sadiq Muhammad Khan Library — IUB Libraries
documents.text: The IUB Libraries, headed by the Sir Sadiq Muhammad Khan Library (SSMK Library), serve as a dynamic hub of knowledge, innovation and academic excellence for the university community. They support the research, teaching and learning needs of students, faculty and researchers with extensive collections, the latest academic materials, digital tools, scholarly articles, research support and quiet, welcoming study spaces, guided by expert library staff.

documents.title: IUB Campuses
documents.source: iub.edu.pk — campus pages (Abbasia, Baghdad-ul-Jadeed, Khwaja Fareed, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan)
documents.text: The Islamia University of Bahawalpur has seven campuses. Abbasia Campus is in a historical building constructed by Nawab Sir Sadiq Muhammad Khan Abbasi-V in the heart of the city near Government Sadiq Egerton College at University Chowk, Bahawalpur (building constructed in 1950). Baghdad-ul-Jadeed Campus (BJC), also known as the Main Campus, is located on Hasilpur Road about eight kilometers from the city center, and most faculties are established there. Khwaja Fareed Campus, on Railway Road, was constructed in 1925 and currently hosts the Faculty of Pharmacy and the Faculty of Medicine and Allied Health Sciences. Sub-campuses: Bahawalnagar (established 2005, Minchanabad Road, spread over 50 acres, 22 teaching departments offering more than 40 undergraduate and postgraduate programmes), Rahim Yar Khan (established 2005, Abu Dhabi Road, spread over 80 acres, 22 teaching departments offering more than 44 programmes), Liaquatpur and Ahmedpur East.
